title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: part of the 1965 'Théorie de Galois des motifs' notes. X is a base, most likely a field such as R or a number field with a real place, and π_1(X) is its Galois or fundamental group. A motive F over X has several realizations, which Grothendieck treats as fibre functors:
- ξ_{X,Z}: the integral Betti realization.
- ξ_{X,R}, ξ_{X,Q}: its real and rational versions.
- ξ_{X,∞}: the complex or 'infinite-place' realization, carrying the Hodge filtration ξ_{X,∞}(F)^ρ.

First paragraph. π_1(X) as a whole does not act on the Betti realizations ξ_{X,Z} or ξ_{X,R}, since Betti cohomology carries no Galois action. Only the decomposition element at the real place does. This is f_∞, the 'Frobenius à l'infini', i.e. complex conjugation acting through the real structure on X(C). It acts on ξ_{X,Z}, hence on ξ_{X,R}, and is extended linearly to ξ_{X,∞} as an operator τ = f_∞.

N.B. on the Hodge conjecture. Grothendieck reads the (generalized) Hodge conjecture as a statement about the arithmetic or motivic filtration 'by level' on rational classes ξ_{X,Q} = ξ_{X,Z}⊗Q. This filtration is induced by sub-motives. The conjecture describes it through the position of the classes relative to the Hodge filtration and to f_∞. Proposed form:
  (level ≤ ρ part of ξ_{X,Q}(F)) = ξ_{X,Q}(F) ∩ ξ_{X,∞}(F)^ρ ∩ f_∞ ξ_{X,∞}(F)^ρ.

The point is that for a real structure, f_∞ extended C-linearly carries F^ρ onto the complex-conjugate filtration F̄^ρ. So the triple intersection is H_Q ∩ F^ρ ∩ F̄^ρ: Hodge's 1950 coniveau statement, rewritten using only motivic or Galois data (the Betti lattice, the Hodge filtration, and the decomposition group at ∞).

It then says: 'in particular' this subspace is motivic, i.e. it is the realization of a sub-motive F^(ρ) of F, as soon as F^ρ and f_∞F^ρ are 'motivic'. The sentence breaks off and the struck lines mention 'two versions of niveau'. The purpose is to place the Hodge conjecture inside the Tannakian 'Galois theory of motives' as a criterion for when a rational subspace comes from a sub-motive.
errors: The displayed criterion is essentially Hodge's original form of the generalized Hodge conjecture (H_Q ∩ F^ρ ∩ F̄^ρ; since H_Q is conjugation-stable this is just H_Q ∩ F^ρ). Grothendieck himself showed in 1969 ('Hodge's general conjecture is false for trivial reasons', Topology 8) that this is false. That Q-subspace need not be a sub-Hodge structure. The corrected statement uses the largest rational sub-Hodge structure whose complexification lies in F^ρ.

Identifying F̄^ρ with f_∞F^ρ requires X (or the motive) to be defined over R, so that F_∞ composed with complex conjugation of coefficients preserves the Hodge decomposition. This hypothesis is not stated.

The closing claim ('the subspace is motivic as soon as F^ρ and f_∞F^ρ are motivic') is ill-defined. F^ρ is a complex subspace, not a rational one, so it cannot be 'motivic' in the stated sense, and the argument is left unfinished.
Indexing: the page writes 'niveau ≤ ρ' together with the Hodge filtration F^ρ. In the usual convention this matches coniveau ≥ ρ, so the indexing is loose.

ideas.what: Only the decomposition element at ∞ (complex conjugation, 'Frobenius infini') acts on the Betti realization of a motive over a real or number field, and it is extended linearly to the complex realization.
ideas.modern_name: F_∞ on Betti cohomology / real Hodge structures (Deligne's 'Valeurs de fonctions L', 1979)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard; systematized by Deligne (1979) for real Hodge structures and periods

ideas.what: Generalized Hodge conjecture phrased as: the motivic level (coniveau) filtration on rational classes equals H_Q ∩ F^ρ ∩ f_∞F^ρ, with the conjugate filtration realized motivically via F_∞.
ideas.modern_name: Generalized Hodge conjecture (Hodge 1950 naive form; Grothendieck 1969 corrected form)
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Hodge's general conjecture is false for trivial reasons', Topology 8 (1969), where he refutes this naive form

ideas.what: The Hodge conjecture viewed as a criterion for a rational subspace of a realization to come from a sub-motive (motivic Galois / Tannakian viewpoint).
ideas.modern_name: Hodge conjecture ⇔ full faithfulness of the Hodge realization on motives (Mumford–Tate group = motivic Galois group)
ideas.where_published: Ideas transmitted through Saavedra Rivano, 'Catégories tannakiennes' (1972), and Serre's writings

missed.claim: Historical detail: in 1965, inside the motivic Galois notes, Grothendieck still endorsed the naive (Hodge 1950) form of the generalized Hodge conjecture, which he publicly refuted in 1969. He also wrote the conjugate filtration as f_∞F^ρ, using the motivic F_∞, rather than as complex conjugation of coefficients.
missed.quote: La partie de niveau ≤ ρ dans ξ_{X,Q}(F) n'est autre que ξ_{X,Q}(F) ∩ ξ_{X,∞}(F)^ρ ∩ f_∞ ξ_{X,∞}(F)^ρ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents the chronology of the 1969 correction and shows the conjecture being framed within Tannakian motivic Galois theory. This is of historical rather than mathematical novelty.

deep.surprise_reason: No new mathematics. The page is mildly interesting historically: it shows Grothendieck in 1965 formulating the generalized Hodge conjecture in its naive form, later refuted by himself, using F_∞ and fibre functors in the motivic Galois setting.
transcription_corrections: 'ni a sur ξ_{X,R}' is probably 'ni même sur ξ_{X,R}'.
'cl. rationnelles de cohomologie' could equally be read 'cl. de cohomologie' / 'classes rationnelles'; the image reads roughly 'les cl. ...'.
'non multiplicative' after 'filtration de Hodge' is uncertain; it may be 'non arithmétique' or 'non rationnelle'.
In the final displayed formula the last term is f_∞ ξ_{X,∞}(F)^ρ; the superscript is written (ρ) inconsistently in the following lines.
